summary: _(c) pass any other order as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit in the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice.”_ - (a) The issue raised in the present Petition does not concern tariff, either directly or indirectly, and clearly falls within the category of non-tariff related dispute, which are subject to arbitration. There is, undisputedly, a valid and subsisting provision for arbitration (Article 14.3.2) in the PPA. Since the dispute in the present case is a non-tariff dispute, the same may be referred to arbitration. - (g) The subject matter of the present Petition does not fall within the adjudicatory jurisdiction of the Commission, and it is to be referred to arbitration. The subject matter falls under the category of non-tariff related disputes that are referable to arbitration in terms of Article 14.3.2.1 of the PPA dated 23.8.2013. APTEL, in its order dated 14.11.2022 in Appeal No. 397/2022 (APSPDCL v. APERC & anr.) has held that the jurisdiction of the Electricity Regulatory Commissions only extends to the tariff-related disputes and that the referral of the non-tariff related disputes to arbitration is mandatory, as otherwise, the arbitration clause is rendered redundant. APTEL also held that the simpliciter money claims, such as Late Payment Surcharge, LD, termination or breach of contract, etc., are non-tariff related disputes and hence, liable to be referred to arbitration. - (s) It is settled by the Hon’ble Supreme Court that where LD stipulated in the contract has been agreed to a genuine and reasonable pre-estimate of the damages, then the contractual position has to be enforced and the party seeking to enforce such provision is not required to prove loss. [reliance is placed on judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in _ONGC v. Saw Pipes_ (2003) 5 SCC 705, _Maula Baux v. UOI_ (1969) 2 SCC 554 and _Construction and Design Services v. DDA_ (2015) 14 SCC 263] **_The contention of TANGEDCO that the issue raised in the present petition does not concern tariff, either directly or indirectly, and clearly falls within the category of non-tariff related disputes, which are subject to arbitration as per Clause 14.3.2.1 of the PPA dated 23.08.2013_** # **_The contention of TANGEDCO that its claims are not time-barred and that it is justified in raising its claims for liquidated damages at this stage_** - (d) Article 14.3.1 provides that where any dispute arises from a claim made by any party for any change in or determination of the tariff or any matter related to the tariff, or claims made by any party which partly or wholly relate to any change in the tariff, the same shall be submitted for adjudication to this Hon’ble Commission exclusively. Also, Article 14.3.2.1 contemplates that Arbitration is only permissible for claims not covered under Article 14.3.1.1; 10. Based on the above submissions of the parties, the issue which emerges for consideration is: _(f) to adjudicate upon disputes involving generating companies or transmission licensee in regard to matters connected with clauses (a) to (d) above and to refer any dispute for arbitration;_ _14.3.1.1 a) where any Dispute arises from a claim made by any Party for any change in or determination of the Tariff or any matter related to Tariff or claims_ _made by any Party which partly or wholly relate to any change in the Tariff or determination of any such claims could result in change in the Tariff shall be submitted to adjudication by the Appropriate Commission. Appeal against the decisions of the Appropriate Commission shall be made only as per the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, as amended from time to time._ - _14.3.2.1 If the Dispute arises out of or in connection with any claims not covered in Article 14.3.1.1 a) such Dispute shall be resolve by arbitration under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and the Rules of the Indian Council of Arbitration, in accordance with the process specified in this Article. In the event of such Dispute remaining unresolved as referred to in Article 14.2.1.3 hereof, any party to such Dispute may refer the matter to Registrar under the Rules of the Indian Counsel of Arbitration . “_ 17. In the present case, there is undisputably a valid and subsisting arbitration clause, i.e., Article 14.3.2.1-quoted in para 14 above- in the PPA. Section 158 of the Act provides that arbitration directed by the Commission shall be subject to the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. Accordingly, the Commission, in line with Section 79(1)(f) and Section 158 of the Act, directs that the present dispute between the parties, including the question of limitation, shall be referred for arbitration. The Commission further directs that both the parties herein, shall within 30 (thirty) days from the date of this order, submit to the Commission, along with an affidavit, their list of two persons, each having relevant knowledge and expertise, for the Commission to choose one (out of the two persons) for appointment as Arbitrator(s) in the present case. While doing so, the parties shall keep in view the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act 2015, order under Section 17 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is passed by the Arbitral tribunal.
title: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for quashing the illegal claim of Rs. 48 crores raised by the Respondent TANGEDCO vide its letter(s) dated 31.7.2024 and 30.9.2024 towards the alleged Liquidated Damages in terms of Article 4.8.1 and 4.8.2 of the PPA dated 23.8.2013 read with the Addendum dated 10.12.2013 and the immediate threat of unilateral deduction of the said amount from the monthly invoice raised by the petitioner, being barred by limitation. Bharat Aluminium Company Limited
